title: Blackstone Steak Sandwiches
shortDescription: Au jus dip energy without the fuss
subtitle: Au jus dip energy without the fuss

steps.title: Simmer au jus (medium, 10 min)
steps.instruction: Prepare jus per packet; keep hot in pitchers. Watch color and texture — if it smells sharp or looks pale, give it another minute before moving on.

steps.title: Bake fries (425°F, 20 min)
steps.instruction: Season fries; bake until crisp. Watch color and texture — if it smells sharp or looks pale, give it another minute before moving on.

steps.title: Build sandwiches (medium, 12 min)
steps.instruction: Warm rolls, pile beef and cheese, brief oven melt if desired.

steps.title: Dress coleslaw (no heat, 5 min)
steps.instruction: Toss slaw; keep cold. Watch color and texture — if it smells sharp or looks pale, give it another minute before moving on.

steps.title: Open dip line (serve)
steps.instruction: Sandwiches, jus cups, fries, and slaw on the counter. Watch color and texture — if it smells sharp or looks pale, give it another minute before moving on.

proTips: Warm rolls before building — cold bread kills the line.
Serve jus in mugs for easy dipping.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold protein after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Plate Blackstone Steak Sandwiches with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Line up Blackstone Steak Sandwiches on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
Store components separate — assemble fresh; buns go soggy overnight.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Au jus dip energy without the fuss. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
